messages.subject: Public-source fee records for your car-buying fee guide
messages.body:
Hello Consumer Reports communications team,

I’m reaching out because Jon Linkov’s guide helps readers distinguish legitimate car-buying charges from dealer add-ons.

DetectHiddenFees reviewed 25 verified public-source records, including CFPB guidance on preparation, document, delivery, market-adjustment, and optional F&I charges. The review is a curated sample, not a market-wide fee study.

The report, methodology, JSON, and CSV are available here:
https://detecthiddenfees.com/research-media-kit

Please consider it only if this source map is useful for readers reviewing vehicle paperwork. No link or coverage is expected.

Best,
DetectHiddenFees Research Team

messages.subject: CFPB source records for your dealer-fee guide
messages.body:
Hello CarEdge press team,

Your guide on dealership fees explains how taxes, title/registration, document fees, and dealer add-ons affect the out-the-door price.

DetectHiddenFees organized 25 verified public-source records, including CFPB and FTC material on preparation, document, delivery, market-adjustment, and optional add-on charges. It is a curated source review, not a market-wide fee study, and it does not replace CarEdge's own dealer-quote data.

The methodology and downloadable records are here:
https://detecthiddenfees.com/research-media-kit

Please use it only if it adds useful source context for readers reviewing dealer paperwork. No coverage or link is expected.

Best,
DetectHiddenFees Research Team

messages.subject: CFPB source map for overdraft-fee terminology

NerdWallet provides provider data, while our review provides source links and bounded consumer-guidance context. It does not replace provider pricing or claim an average.

Please use it only if it helps readers inspect their account terms.
